slides.texte_overlay:
Ways to feel calmly sure of
yourself in any room
Prepare one thing to talk about before you go. A trip, a book, something funny from your week. Knowing you have a story ready removes half the nerves.
Find one familiar face first. Say hello to the host or a friend before anyone else. Starting with someone you know gives you a warm, safe base in the room.
Ask people questions about themselves. Most people are nervous too. Taking the spotlight off yourself and onto them relaxes everyone, including you.
Feed your confidence from the inside. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and knowing I've always got something to offer keeps me calm in any room.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Knowing I've always got something to offer keeps me calm in any room.

slides.texte_overlay: Wear something you feel great in. Not new, not flashy, just your best fit. When you're not thinking about your clothes, you're free to think about people.
Accept that not everyone will love you. Some people won't click with you, and that's fine. Letting go of pleasing everyone is where real calm confidence starts.
Leave on a high note. Say goodbye while you're still enjoying yourself. Walking out happy makes you remember the evening as a success, and so do others.
